request: Externally source exactly 150 materially distinct, budget-conscious complete dinner recipes from verifiable public recipe pages. Hard per-serving nutrition limits: each complete served meal must contain at least 500 and at most 650 calories, inclusive, and no more than 35 grams total carbohydrates. Do not accept a recipe unless the source publishes a complete ingredient list, a usable yield, and per-serving calories and total carbohydrates that verify those limits; reject instead of estimating missing source nutrition. Every recipe must be a complete meal containing both a main and a substantial included accompaniment that is part of the source serving and nutrition basis. Standalone protein preparations do not qualify. Aromatics, garnish, sauce, broth, cooking fat, and seasoning do not count as an accompaniment. The mapped substantial accompaniment must provide at least 70 grams per serving. Scale qualified recipes to the standard 14-serving meal-prep batch only after preserving the published source quantities and yield. Exclude all seafood and all ground-chicken recipes. Favor common affordable grocery ingredients and broad diversity across cuisines, cooking methods, protein classes, vegetarian meals, and low-carbohydrate vegetable accompaniments; avoid superficial title variations and near-duplicates of one concept. Verify every external URL and record its access timestamp. Every final candidate must independently satisfy every constraint; do not pad the count with unverified or borderline recipes.
